items.title: Finding the Area of a Triangle Given Its Base and Height

sections.normalized_html: A triangle has a base length of [MATH: 12] feet and a height of [MATH: 90] feet. What is the area, in square feet, of the triangle?

To find the area of a triangle, we use the formula [MATH: A = \frac{1}{2} \cdot b \cdot h,] where [MATH: b] is the base length and [MATH: h] is the height.

items.title: Finding the Area of a Right Triangle Given Its Legs

sections.normalized_html:
Note: Figure not drawn to scale.

The figure shows the lengths, in meters, of two sides of a right triangle. What is the area of the triangle, in square meters?
sections.readable_text:
[IMG: /graphics/16b4bf1688c81544dd84c74a6f4a1e00]

Note: Figure not drawn to scale.

The figure shows the lengths, in meters, of two sides of a right triangle. What is the area of the triangle, in square meters?

sections.normalized_html:
In a right triangle, we can use the two legs as the base and the height because they are perpendicular.

We are given that the legs have lengths [MATH: 10] meters and [MATH: 4] meters.

We use the area formula for a triangle: [MATH: A = \frac{1}{2} \cdot \text{base} \cdot \text{height}]

Now, we substitute the values: [MATH: A|= (1)/(2) ⋅ 10 ⋅ 4; = (1)/(2) ⋅ 40; = 20m^{2}]

So, the area of the triangle is [MATH: 20 \, \textrm{m}^2.]
